title: Safety Design
summary: Hardware protection invariants, forbidden commands, build-plate arming, and fail-closed behavior.

content.text: Plain summary

The safety design assumes people make mistakes and software fails. The printer should stop heaters and refuse work before it accepts unknown state. Convenience features are allowed only when they fail before hardware protections are weakened.
Pressure advance and extrusion accounting

Orca may set nonzero pressure advance only while Klipper is actively running a protected, admitted print snapshot. The only accepted form is SET_PRESSURE_ADVANCE ADVANCE=value, where value is finite and between 0 and 0.20. Runtime smooth-time changes, alternate extruders, unknown parameters, and uploaded TUNING_TOWER are blocked. START_PRINT, END_PRINT, and cancellation reset pressure advance to zero so one filament cannot leak tuning into the next job. A paused admitted print may issue only the zero reset; this lets cancellation complete without allowing paused tuning changes.

Retraction credit follows a simple rule: pulling filament back earns only that much credit, and a stationary recovery spends it. Normal moving extrusion clears stale credit. Orca writes E values to five decimal places, so exact decimal accounting allows only the discrepancy mathematically explainable by the number of rounded retract and wipe segments, with at most 64 segments in one recovery. Another rounding exception requires real moving deposition. Across the file, rounding-only stationary extrusion is limited to one hundred-thousandth of actual moving extrusion plus one 0.0001 mm startup/path allowance. There is no fixed whole-file ceiling that would reject a legitimate large print merely for having more layers. E-only use, malformed precision, excessive per-event discrepancy, repeated stationary use, or microscopic moves used to farm allowance fail.

The scanner and Klipper divide responsibility deliberately. The scanner rejects attempts to raise velocity or acceleration ceilings and rejects coordinates outside the machine envelope. A raw G1 feed request is still clamped by Klipper's immutable runtime max_velocity. This keeps ordinary Orca speed calibration possible without allowing G-code to raise the hardware ceiling.
Safety layer boundaries
Klipper core remains responsible for sensors, heaters, endstops, MCU communication, watchdog behavior, and emergency stop.
The custom t300_safety extra does not replace heater or motion control. It rejects unsafe commands, clamps runtime limits, and controls the build-plate readiness state.
Macros can request actions, but they cannot raise hard ceilings for temperature, velocity, acceleration, current, or extrusion limits.
Uploaded G-code is scanned and then copied into a protected snapshot before Klipper may print it.
Failure paths turn heaters off before optional parking, UI prompts, timelapse cleanup, or notifications.

attrs.title: provide more details
attrs.instruction: this still reads like a summary. I'd like a clear list of the behaviour changes and safety changes you implemented especially also what you classified as "unsafe behaviour" etc.  And what kind of print limits.
attrs.resolution: Expanded in this page with implemented behavior changes, unsafe-behavior classes, and the concrete production print limits from the candidate policy.

content.text: Implemented behavior changes
These are candidate behavior changes in the repository. They are not active on the live printer until the owner performs the recovery, install, and commissioning gates.

Print startup requires the build plate to be marked clean and rearmed before heat or motion. The check is consumed by print startup and becomes required again after printing, purging, hot filament handling, cancellation, errors, Klipper restart, or shutdown.
Uploaded or USB G-code is scanned first, then copied into a protected read-only snapshot. Klipper prints the approved snapshot, not the mutable uploaded file.
Orca files must contain object definitions before one START_PRINT call and one END_PRINT call. Missing object data is refused because the purge lane cannot be chosen safely.

START_PRINT uses a 150 C nozzle standby, heats the bed, homes through the normal probe path, runs a full 9x9 mesh, parks, finishes nozzle heating, then performs KAMP moving purge. There is no stationary positive blob purge.
END_PRINT and CANCEL_PRINT retract only while Klipper says extrusion is hot enough, shut heaters down, lift before XY travel, and park at or above Z 200 only when axes and clearance are known.
Normal idle after ten minutes turns heaters and the part-cooling fan off, while leaving motors enabled so the gantry is not released as a side effect of heater safety.
Runout pauses once. M600, load, and unload are attended workflows: they require pause state, hot-enough extrusion, bounded filament movement, and they mark the plate dirty again.

Production preserves complete upstream Mainsail and the exact stock serial-touchscreen layout. The touchscreen's unprivileged bridge can reach only a constrained loopback gateway; the command policy, immutable limits, and native Klipper checks remain the real guards.
Maintenance is a separate local-only configuration. There is no G-code command that switches production into maintenance mode.
Vendor power-loss recovery paths are disabled in the candidate because they can invent position or restart stale state after an interruption.
Unsafe behavior classification

I classified behavior as unsafe when it can bypass a sensor, invent state, raise a reviewed hardware limit, move or extrude without enough context, mutate the machine while a print could be active, or hide a failure that should stop the printer.

Fake or forced motion state: FORCE_MOVE, SET_KINEMATIC_POSITION, raw G28 inside print files, direct PROBE commands, direct bed-mesh commands from print files, and Z or gantry calibration commands in production print files.

Direct thermal or pin control: raw heater/object-pin commands, temperature targets above policy, malformed temperature commands, heater verification failures, invalid sensor readings, and scripts that try to keep cleanup running after a heater fault.
Driver and current bypasses: raw TMC register writes, unapproved steppers, current above the verified factory currents, and direct stepper enable/disable commands from prints.

Unbounded extrusion: cold extrusion, E-only moves over the limit, positive stationary extrusion without matching retraction credit, extrusion cross-section over the policy limit, malformed relative extrusion after an unknown position, or flow overrides above 100 percent.

Host or firmware mutation: SAVE_CONFIG, shell commands, firmware restart/write paths, config writes, legacy power-loss resume, symlinks, files that change while being scanned, and uploads that exceed file or storage limits.

Lifecycle bypasses: more than one START_PRINT or END_PRINT, commands after END_PRINT, object definitions after START_PRINT, missing object data, direct KAMP/mesh/purge calls from the file, or a purge lane too close to the model.

Operator trapdoors: Z or all-axis homing while a print is loaded or paused, Z or all-axis homing without a fresh clean-and-rearmed plate state, assuming a failed X/Y-only home is harmless, upload-and-print shortcuts, and treating ordinary queued Cancel as the emergency path.
Important exception: live M112 Emergency Stop remains untouched and immediate. A print file may not contain M112 because a queued file should not be the way emergency shutdown is triggered.
Production print limits
The limits below are the candidate policy ceilings. Runtime commands may lower them, but production G-code may not raise them.

File and storage limits: one admitted file up to 512 MiB, lines up to 5,000,000, each line up to 16 KiB, up to 1,024 candidate files, approved spool storage up to 1 GiB, at least 1 GiB of system free space, and up to 10,000 timelapse frame requests.
Object data limits: up to 4,096 objects, up to 2,048 polygon points per object, up to 65,536 total object points, and all object coordinates must be finite and inside the configured bed bounds.

Temperature and heater limits: nozzle targets 0..300 C, START_PRINT nozzle 150..300 C, bed targets 0..100 C, minimum extrusion floor 150 C, hotend max_power 1.0, bed max_power 1.0, with Klipper heater verification still active.

Motion limits: X -2..302 mm, Y -6..302 mm, Z -5..370 mm, max velocity 600 mm/s, max acceleration 12000 mm/s2, max Z velocity 12 mm/s, max Z acceleration 100 mm/s2, square-corner velocity at most 3 mm/s, and minimum_cruise_ratio cannot be lowered below 0.75.
Motor-current limits: X 1.1 A, Y 1.5 A, Z 0.75 A, and extruder 1.0 A. SET_TMC_CURRENT may target only approved steppers and may not exceed those values.

Extrusion limits: max_extrude_cross_section 5 mm2, E-only distance 100 mm, E-only velocity 2000 mm/s, E-only acceleration 10000 mm/s2, instantaneous extruder corner velocity 10, and filament diameter 1.75 mm. Stationary recovery is no longer a generic 5 mm allowance: it may only repay filament that the same print previously retracted, with tightly bounded allowances for Orca's decimal rounding.
Override limits: M220 and M221 may reduce speed or flow but may not exceed 100 percent. G4 dwell is capped at 60 seconds.
Commands blocked in production

The production path forbids commands that can bypass the normal model of the printer: force movement, inventing positions, raw heater or output control, unrestricted TMC fields, shell commands, firmware writes, config writes, manual motor release, direct probing commands, and legacy power-loss resume paths.
Build-plate checkmark workflow

Before a Z home or print, the operator confirms in Mainsail that the magnetic sheet is installed, flat, clipped, clean, and clear of loose filament. The confirmation survives harmless idle actions and a successful X/Y-only home, but it is consumed or invalidated by printing, purging, hot extrusion, filament load or unload, M600, cancellation, any failed home, Klipper restart, and loaded-print errors.

The check cannot be set while a print is loaded or paused, while the hotend has any target temperature, or while the hotend is at extrusion temperature. This prevents rearming during a hot, filament-processing state.
Important limitation

This is not a physical sheet sensor. If a human confirms the sheet and then removes it, software cannot know. A real plate-presence sensor is the only hardware-grade fix for the missing-sheet accident class.
